issues.legal_issue: A testamentary gift to a daughter followed by a direction that the property pass to her male children gives the daughter only a life interest, not an absolute estate.
material_facts: The will provided that the testator’s wife would enjoy the properties during her lifetime, then the daughter would enjoy them, and after the daughter they would go to her male children.
The High Court construed the daughter’s interest as a life estate, with the male children taking the properties absolutely after her death.
issues.conclusion: The daughter acquired only a life interest because the direction that the properties pass to her male children after her showed that the testator did not intend to give her an absolute estate; the High Court’s construction was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: In construing a will, effect should be given to each disposition so far as legally possible. A clear direction that property pass to another beneficiary after the first beneficiary’s death negates an intention to give the first beneficiary an absolute estate. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_will_construction: The proceeding is an appeal in which the court must determine the construction of a will.
predicates.will_gives_beneficiary_enjoyment_then_re: The will gives a beneficiary enjoyment of property and directs that it pass to the beneficiary’s descendants after that beneficiary’s death.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a will that gives a beneficiary enjoyment of property and directs that it pass to the beneficiary’s descendants after the beneficiary’s death, the beneficiary has only a life interest.

issues.legal_issue: A ground not raised in the courts below or in a petition for special leave cannot be raised for the first time during argument in the appeal.
material_facts: During argument in the appeal, the appellant contended that an interest which was only for life under the will had become absolute under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
The contention had not been raised in the courts below or in the petition for special leave.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not permit the appellant to raise the contention for the first time during argument in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal by special leave under Article 136 of the Constitution, a contention not raised in the courts below or in the petition for special leave cannot be raised for the first time during argument. The Court did not decide whether Section 14(1) applied on the merits.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and ground_not_raised_below and ground_not_in_special_leave_petition and ground_first_raised_during_argument

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.ground_not_raised_below: The party did not raise the ground in the courts below.
predicates.ground_not_in_special_leave_petition: The party did not include the ground in the petition for special leave.
predicates.ground_first_raised_during_argument: The party first raised the ground during argument in the appeal.

issues.definition: In a special leave appeal, a ground omitted from the proceedings below and the special leave petition, and first raised during argument, is not entertained.
